findings.summary: Request-scoped sessions could leave an implicit transaction open until close.
findings.evidence_before: get_db() yielded SessionLocal() and only called close() in finally.
findings.fix: get_db() now rolls back on exceptions and ManagedSession.close() rolls back any still-open transaction before close.

findings.summary: Direct SessionLocal context managers needed the same orphan transaction protection as request dependencies.
findings.evidence_before: Middleware and service code use with SessionLocal() for bounded database work.
findings.fix: SessionLocal now creates ManagedSession, so context manager exit performs rollback-before-close protection globally.

findings.summary: SQLAlchemy sessions were reusable after close by default.
findings.fix: SessionLocal now uses close_resets_only=false to make closed sessions final and prevent cross-request reuse.

findings.summary: Middleware should not hold database sessions across downstream request handling.
findings.result: Reviewed middleware SessionLocal usages are bounded in with blocks and end before call_next continues.

request_lifecycle_after_fix.normal_exit: db.close() invokes ManagedSession.close(), rolling back any uncommitted transaction and releasing the connection.
request_lifecycle_after_fix.exception_exit: get_db() explicitly rolls back before re-raising, then closes in finally.
request_lifecycle_after_fix.closed_session_reuse: Rejected by SQLAlchemy InvalidRequestError because close_resets_only=false.

commit_rollback_assessment.terminal_rollback_guard: All SessionLocal sessions now receive rollback-before-close cleanup for uncommitted or orphan transactions.
commit_rollback_assessment.reason: This fixes connection lifecycle leakage without changing API behavior or business transaction boundaries.

residual_risk: Streaming or long-running request responses still release dependency sessions at framework finalization time; the finalizer now rolls back and closes deterministically.
Injected existing sessions in service helpers remain owned by their caller; caller-owned request sessions are covered by get_db().
